correctness.rationale: The diagonal C* action has exactly the degree-d monomial points as ambient projective fixed points. A monomial x^(d-s)y^s belongs to the coincident root locus if a subset of the prescribed multiplicity parts sums to s; conversely, unique factorization forces every linear factor in a monomial factorization to be proportional to x or y. Thus the fixed locus has exactly |Sigma(lambda)| reduced points. Euler localization applies without smoothness assumptions, and projectivity converts compactly supported Euler characteristic to ordinary Euler characteristic. The ambient-equality criterion is proved by interval induction. The checker independently replays all finite combinatorics over a broad partition range.

value.rationale: Coincident root loci are classical singular projective varieties central to binary-form discriminants and multiple-root geometry. The theorem converts their ordinary Euler characteristic into a transparent additive invariant of the multiplicity partition, revealing a structural contrast with Hilbert's multiplicative projective-degree formula. The complete-sequence corollary gives an exact classification of when a proper multiple-root locus is Euler-indistinguishable from the whole ambient projective space. This is an all-partition structural classification rather than a finite or arbitrarily sliced computation.
